memoryFile.header:
# VEMRY.md — conventions for this vault

This file is injected into the AI agent's system prompt: it is the constitution it reads to understand this vault.
memoryFile.template:
Describe your structure and preferences in your own words, for example:

## Structure
- `inbox.md`: quick capture — unsorted thoughts land here first
- `projects/`: work in progress, one map-of-content note per project
- `daily/`: journal

## Conventions
- Tags: #idea #reading #todo
- Linking: create a [[link]] the first time a concept appears
- AI preferences: say what you intend before editing a note; put surveys in `reviews/`
memoryPrompt.draft:
Draft VEMRY.md for this vault — it is the constitution injected into your system prompt, and you read it at the start of every turn from now on.

Survey before you write: browse the folder structure and how tags are actually used, sample a few representative notes, and infer the real habits around naming, linking and organisation (do not invent what you are unsure of).

Then create VEMRY.md with write_note. Requirements:
- Short (under 50 lines), conventions and preferences only; the folder list and tag counts are already injected into the system prompt, so do not repeat them
- Suggested sections: Structure (what each directory and key note is for), Conventions (tags, links, naming habits), AI behaviour preferences
- Anything you are unsure about goes in a closing “To confirm” section as questions for me to answer
memoryPrompt.review: Review VEMRY.md: read it, then use your tools to check it against the vault as it is now — is anything out of date, has a new habit formed that is worth recording, is anything long-winded enough to trim? Propose changes with edit_note if there are any (keep it short); if it is still accurate, say so.
